rv.q: In its utter disregard for the mundane, it ends up showing us more of the truth of its performer.
It is a resurrection, and it is glorious.

I am, admittedly, more readily charmed by puppets than some, but Arias with a Twist really does offer multiple angles from which to enjoy it: the ingenuity and razzle-dazzle of Twist’s effects; stagecraft that gives plenty of opportunities for transformation even within a tiny space; the architecture of a classic cabaret show; and the tongue—and...
The result is enchanting variety, which makes time pass quickly.
Arias and Twist have created a show of pure imagination and unapologetic delight.
Still, I wonder if the team erred in replicating Twist so exactly, like a museum piece on display.
This colorful cabaret from another dimension takes us on a delightful, genre-bending journey from inter-galactic drama to a garden of earthly delights.
For all its outrageous humor and sensory overload, Arias with a Twist felt like a complete celebration of performing art.
Imagination is off the charts; manifestation virtuosic.
I’m happy to report that it has lost none of its transgressive power.
This exuberant collaboration has lost none of its capacity to surprise.

More story by association than cogent narrative, creators Arias and Twist have again brought the fun, laughs, theatricality, imagination, wonder, naughtiness, and coloring-outside-the-lines sensibility that made the show a success almost twenty years ago.
But the vocals fall short, evoking feelings that I didn't want to be having at a show with such a warm glam glow.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this imaginative downtown spectacle as a triumphant return, praising Joey Arias' magnetic performance and Basil Twist's eye-popping puppetry for creating a wildly original theatrical fantasia that has lost none of its joyful strangeness.

vr.q: Part of the joy of watching this show is just being amazed with the craft, the theatricality that they've created in this tiny little space.
